title: Avo's cookbook
about: Recipes from public US government recipe pages, every one opened on 2026-10-09 and credited to its page. Quantities, servings and times are the source's; steps are short and in our own words. No prices.

rules.vegetarian: No meat, poultry, fish or shellfish in the ingredients (optional ones left out).
rules.vegan: Vegetarian, and no egg, milk or honey.
rules.gluten-free: No wheat, barley or rye in the ingredients. Oats, broth and sauces still need a gluten-free label (check_labels).
rules.dairy-free: No milk, cheese, yogurt, butter or cream.
rules.low-sodium: The source gives 140 mg sodium or less per serving (the FDA label term "low sodium").
rules.diabetes-friendly: Keeps to the pattern on my diabetes card: no red or processed meat, no refined grains, no added sugar. Not a carb count: a personal carb target is a dietitian's job.
rules.high-protein: The source gives 20 g of protein or more per serving (the low end of the per-meal dose on my protein card).
rules.kid-friendly: The source itself says it is for kids or the family.
rules.allergens: The nine major US food allergens found in the ingredients; optional_allergens come only from optional ingredients. Always read the label of every packaged item.

recipes.title: Baked French Toast
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and spray a rimmed baking sheet with nonstick spray.
Microwave the butter on high until melted, about 15-30 seconds, and let it cool slightly.
In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, vanilla, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Whisk in the cooled butter and the milk.
Pour the egg mixture onto the baking sheet and tilt the pan so it covers the bottom.
Quickly lay the bread in a single layer, flip each slice, and let soak 1-2 minutes.
Bake until the bottoms are golden-brown, about 12-15 minutes.
Leave the pan in the oven and switch to broil on high until the tops are lightly browned, about 1-3 minutes; watch closely.
Serve warm.

recipes.title: Baked Pumpkin Oatmeal

ingredients.item: pumpkin pie spice or ground cinnamon

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Spray an 8x8-inch baking dish or a 12-cup muffin tin with nonstick spray.
In a large bowl, stir together the oats, brown sugar, spice, baking powder and salt.
Add the pumpkin and eggs and stir until the eggs are mixed in.
Stir in the milk and vanilla.
Spoon the mixture into the baking dish or divide it among the muffin cups.
Bake until fully set: about 30-35 minutes in the dish or 25-30 minutes in the muffin tin; the center should be firm when tapped.
Cool 5 minutes before slicing or removing from the tin, then serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Banana-Oatmeal Protein Pancakes
steps: Mash the banana with a fork in a medium bowl.
Mix in the eggs until well combined.
Optional: blend rolled oats in a blender or food processor until finely ground; skip this for quick-cooking oats.
Stir the oats and cinnamon into the banana mixture.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat, add the oil, and heat until shimmering.
Scoop the batter in 1/4-cup portions around the pan, leaving at least 1/2 inch between them.
Cook until golden-brown on the first side, about 1-3 minutes.
Flip the pancakes and cook until golden-brown on the other side, about 1-2 minutes.
Repeat with any remaining batter and serve warm with toppings as desired.

steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and black pepper with a fork in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, add the oil, and heat until shimmering.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and bell pepper, stirring often, until tender and lightly browned, about 3-5 minutes.
Move the vegetables to a plate.
Spray the pan, return it to the stove, and lower the heat to medium-low.
Pour in the egg mixture and cover the pan with a lid.
Cook without stirring until firm but still moist, about 2-4 minutes.

Turn off the heat, cover, and let the cheese melt, about 2-3 minutes; serve warm.

recipes.title: Garden-Fresh Gazpacho

ingredients.prep: peeled, seeded, and finely chopped (about 1 cup)

steps: Fill a large pot halfway with water and bring it to a boil over high heat.

Let them cool about 1 minute until easy to handle, then lift out and pat dry.

steps: In a saucepan, bring the water, sugar, lemon juice and lemon peel (and rum or vanilla if using) to a boil, then lower the heat, add the fruit and cook on very low heat 5 minutes.
Pour the syrup into a cup and set it aside; remove the lemon peel and let the cooked fruit cool for 2 hours.
Arrange the fruit in a serving dish, spoon a few teaspoons of syrup over it, and garnish with mint if you like.

prep.reheat: Reheat to 165°F on a food thermometer; bring soups and sauces to a rolling boil (USDA FSIS).
